summary: Explains that Ansible runs tasks synchronously by default, holding the connection open and blocking the next task, which can cause SSH timeouts or prevent background work. Asynchronous mode controls how long-running tasks run.
questions: Why does my long task time out over SSH?
Can I run a long task in the background while other tasks continue?
Does Ansible wait for each task to finish before starting the next?

answer_card.title: Why use asynchronous mode
answer_card.answer_md: By default tasks run synchronously: Ansible keeps the connection open until the action completes, and each task blocks the next. A task can then outlast the SSH session and time out, or you can't run a long process in the background while doing other work. Asynchronous mode (`async`/`poll`) lets you control how long-running tasks execute.
